newsitem.title: USA: Converse CFO backs analysts' 1997 forecast.
newsitem.headline: Converse CFO backs analysts' 1997 forecast.

text.p: Converse Inc said on Thursday it will meet, and possibly exceed, analysts' consensus estimate of net income per share of $0.50 for fiscal 1997.
"If the momentum keeps up, that's probably on the conservative side," Chief Financial Officer Donald Camacho said in an interview during the annual Super Show, a sports exposition.

He also agreed with analysts' estimates that the company would post a net loss per share of $0.30 for the fourth quarter of 1996, which would translate into a net loss of $0.80 per share for the entire year.
Earlier, in a speech to securities analysts at the show, Converses Chief Executive Glenn Rupp said, "We're on the mend and we're turning around."

Rupp, who became CEO last year, attributed the company's problems to mistakes made in the introduction of new footwear. He added that the All-Star 2000 shoe introduced late last year is selling well, and that Converse expects a boost from signing Dennis Rodman, the controversial Chicago Bulls basketball star, to endorse its products.
